descriptions.Nebula Rise: A deep-space build, par 71 at 6,592 yards, from Pob16, who also made the sim's Cape Kidnappers and The National. That is the argument for it: the premise is science fiction, but the hand that drew the holes has serious work behind it.
descriptions.Outpost 87: Golf on a military outpost in a universe that is Starship Troopers in all but name, down to the United Citizen Federation on the location line. Par 72 at 7,025 yards, which makes it a full round rather than a diorama. Simulator only.
descriptions.Riverwalk Skills Challenge: Not a golf course. Twelve skill-challenge holes: pick a distance, hit the target, score on accuracy, with Long Drive, Break Glass and Flop Shot games alongside. The most genuinely useful thing in this section for a practice hour, and the easiest thing to put in front of somebody who has never hit a ball.
descriptions.Rock Bay Golf Club: An invented stretch of California coast, par 72 at 7,059 yards, built to pass for a real course rather than to look like a fantasy. There is no reference to get and nothing to recognise, which is the appeal: it plays as though it had been sitting there for decades.
descriptions.Sanctuary Moon: Endor, from Star Wars, and the most watched course in GSPro. R2-D2, C-3PO and an Ewok are in it. Mountain golf at 7,254 yards, built at full length, so the round holds up once the novelty has gone. Searching "Sanctuary" rather than "Star" is the way to find it.
descriptions.Sasquatch Canyon: Mountain golf set above Park City, Utah, with whatever the name promises somewhere out in the trees. Short at 5,894 yards against a par of 69, which makes it a quicker round than most of the mountain builds. Simulator only.
descriptions.Scary Acres: The second of the Halloween builds and the small one: par 27 over 1,237 yards, so nine short holes rather than a full round. Horror scenery, wedges and a putter, forty minutes. Simulator only, and a companion to Course of the Dead rather than a rival to it.
descriptions.TGL Platform Golf: TGL is the indoor arena league Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy set up through TMRW Sports, played against a screen at the SoFi Center in Palm Beach Gardens. This build turns that back into an outdoor course, so it is a simulator rendering of a simulator league. Par 72, 7,343 yards.
descriptions.The Globe: Fictional, by schurlette, and at 8,303 yards against a par of 73 the longest thing in GSPro by a wide margin. The length is the entire proposition: a round here is a test of how far the clubs go. Simulator only, and worth loading once for the numbers alone.
descriptions.The Old Game: An invented Scottish links from Carl's Place, par 72 at 6,768 yards, named after what the game used to be called. Picked out in the SGT room in October 2026 as the best course going, which is unusual company for a build of somewhere that does not exist. Simulator only.
descriptions.Tongass National: Set in Alaskan rainforest, which is a real landscape: the Tongass is the largest national forest in the United States. The routing is invented. Coastal, par 72, 6,674 yards, and a build the review channels keep returning to. The one course in this group with no joke attached to it.
descriptions.Treasure Island: Robert Louis Stevenson's island as eighteen holes. Coastal, par 72 at 6,879 yards. The source is a novel rather than a film, so the look of the place is the builder's reading of it; what arrives is a playable course with pirate dressing. Simulator only.
descriptions.Twisted Sticks Golf Club: The full-length half of a pair set in Newland, North Carolina. Mountain golf, par 72 at 6,512 yards, with the build's own fiction casting the place as a private club lost in time. Simulator only, and the one to load when the pitch and putt has been exhausted.
descriptions.Waterworld: A par 72 built on platforms, with fairways and greens sitting six metres above open water and nothing at all either side of them. That punishes a wide tee shot absolutely rather than relatively, which is the whole character of the round. 7,479 yards, simulator only.
descriptions.Whispering Pines: An invented mountain course, exclusive to GSPro, and the name that comes up first whenever somebody asks which course to play. Par 72 at 7,006 yards, and still listed among the kinder rounds in the book despite the length. Simulator only.
descriptions.Pine Valley (Short): Pine Valley's ten-hole short course, opened in 1992: the idea came from the club president, Ernie Ransome, and the design from Tom Fazio. Eight of the holes reproduce approach shots from the big course and two are new. Ransome wanted ten so that a five-hole Nassau would work. A warm-up at the club that admits almost nobody.
descriptions.Payne's Valley 19th: One hole, kept as a separate course from Payne's Valley itself: the bonus 19th at Big Cedar Lodge, an island green ringed by limestone with a waterfall coming down the rock behind it. It was Johnny Morris's idea rather than Tiger Woods's, and it exists to settle bets. In the sim it is a closest-to-the-pin contest and nothing more.
descriptions.RTJ Sr. Miniature Championship: A Robert Trent Jones Sr. short course for the Country Club of Detroit in Grosse Pointe, approved by the board in 1964 and dated by most directories to 1966. Plateau greens ringed with deep bunkers, on flat ground and an easy walk. At 2,774 yards here it needs more than wedges, which is rare in this section.
descriptions.3s Greenville: A par-3 course in Greenville built on the site of CrossWinds, a 1997 layout that Jeff Lawrence redrew and reopened in 2020. Floodlit into the night, which is the purpose of the place: a short round after work with a wedge and a putter rather than a day out. Justin Timberlake is among the investors.
descriptions.401 Par Golf (Par 3 Course): A nine-hole par 3 in south Raleigh, dating to 1972 and credited to Harry Dupree. The holes run from about 50 to 115 yards, so it is wedge golf from first to last: a municipal short course for getting a round in before dark. Typing "401 Par" is enough to find it.
descriptions.Armco Park: A company park turned public course in Warren County, Ohio, named for Armco Steel, which once owned the ground. Par 57 over 3,028 yards, and the greens run at stimp 8 to 10, slower than anything else in the catalogue. That makes it the gentlest round in the book and a sensible place to start a guest.
descriptions.Bellair Golf Park Executive: A 1972 executive course in Glendale, Arizona, par 59 at 3,421 yards. More than half the holes are par 4s and the greens are heavily bunkered, so most of the bag gets used rather than just a wedge and a putter. Ninety minutes rather than a full afternoon.
descriptions.Casserly Par 3: A nine-hole par 3 outside Watsonville, opened in 1966 by Bob Sanford, who funded it with an avocado orchard and built it with his sons. The family still runs it: cheap, unpretentious and aimed at beginners. KFG's rebuild is the only short course in the book that asks for firm links turf.
descriptions.Double Eagle Par 3: The nine-hole par 3 at the Double Eagle Club in Galena, Ohio, a private club founded by John H. McConnell whose main course is a Weiskopf and Morrish design from the early 1990s. The short course opened in October 2019. A quick loop at a place almost nobody gets to see.
descriptions.Georgia Threes: A nine-hole par 3 in the Augusta idiom, par 27 over 1,067 yards. This is the little course rather than the sim's Georgia Golf Club, so the round is short irons, wedges and a putter, and comfortably under an hour. Reasonable as a warm-up before the long one.
descriptions.Gleneagles: The Canadian Gleneagles: a municipal nine in West Vancouver that opened in 1927 and has belonged to the district since 1958, with A. V. Macan credited for the layout. Named after the Scottish resort and taking cues from its King's Course, but short at 5,214 yards and with no Ryder Cup attached.
descriptions.Jester Park Par 3: The nine-hole par 3 at Jester Park, a Polk County Conservation complex north of Des Moines that also runs an eighteen-hole course, a practice ground and a mini golf. 1,145 yards in total here, which is wedges and a putter and nothing else. A quick nine for somebody starting out.
descriptions.Jug Mountain Mini 9: A short par-3 loop beside the practice ground at Jug Mountain Ranch, a mountain golf property at McCall in the Idaho highlands. Despite the name it is real golf rather than mini golf, played with wedges, and the right thing for the hour before dinner.
descriptions.Mattaponi Springs Short: A short, par-54 version of Mattaponi Springs, the public course between Richmond and Fredericksburg that Bob Lohmann and Mike Benkusky laid out on rolling Virginia ground in 2004, and Lohmann's first work on the East Coast. 2,689 yards here: a short round rather than a pitch and putt.
descriptions.Mountain Top: Thirteen par 3s on a rocky plateau at Big Cedar Lodge in the Missouri Ozarks, by Gary Player Design with Johnny Morris. Walking only, limestone outcrops through the routing, and holes from under a hundred yards to well over two hundred. PurePlay are building it as well, so a direct comparison is coming.
descriptions.Navy GC – Cruiser: The nine-hole executive course at the Navy golf complex in Cypress, California, which opened in 1966 alongside the eighteen-hole Destroyer. This is the complex where Tiger Woods learned the game as a small child. At 4,028 yards it is the longest of the short courses in the book.
descriptions.Needwood Executive 9: The nine-hole executive course at Needwood in Derwood, Maryland, a Montgomery County public site where Lindsay Ervin drew both layouts; most listings date this one to 1985. Seven par 3s and two par 4s. A step up from pitch and putt, and still comfortably inside an hour.
descriptions.Olympic Club (Cliffs): The Olympic Club's nine-hole par 3, laid out on the bluffs above the Pacific and above the Lake Course, which takes all of the attention. Short holes on the cliff edge with the ocean behind them. A warm-up or an evening nine at a club whose reputation rests entirely on the big course.
descriptions.Rancho Park Par 3: A nine-hole par 3 sharing a site with Rancho Park, the Los Angeles municipal course that hosted the LA Open seventeen times. Holes of 82 to 148 yards, tree-lined and busy from first light. City golf without pretension, and the same ground doubles as a footgolf course.
descriptions.The Short Course at Mountain Shadows: Eighteen par 3s under Camelback Mountain. It began as Arthur Jack Snyder's 1961 executive course for the Mountain Shadows resort and was rebuilt as an all-par-3 layout by Forrest Richardson, who had worked for Snyder early in his career. Holes of roughly 60 to 200 yards, and among the best-regarded short courses in America.
descriptions.Top of the Rock: Jack Nicklaus's par-3 course at Big Cedar Lodge, laid out with Johnny Morris above Table Rock Lake, with a short signature hole that drops a hundred feet to the green. It hosted the Bass Pro Shops Legends of Golf from 2014 to 2019, which made it a rarity: a par-3 course staging professional golf.
descriptions.Virginia Golf Center Par 3: The nine-hole par 3 at a practice centre in Clifton, Virginia, dating to 1998 and sitting beside double-deck range bays, a short-game area and a Toptracer range. Unglamorous, with small greens, and exactly the kind of round that fits into an hour after work.
descriptions.Battle Group Par 3's: Par 3s on a warship, which is the premise and all of it. The location line on the real listing reads CLASSIFIED, and the build keeps the joke up throughout. Tropical, par 54, and eighteen short holes, so the novelty does not have to last long. Simulator only.
descriptions.Canyon Run (Par 3): An invented desert par 3, named on the GSPro Discord as the best of its kind in the game. Short holes over canyon ground, par 54, with a full-length sibling for afterwards. Simulator only, and the one for an hour rather than an afternoon.
descriptions.Chaos Cove: 2,978 yards of deliberate nonsense from CDrum: par 63, soft greens, soft fairways, soft everything, built for amusement rather than scoring. Not a round to take a handicap to. Simulator only, and the right thing to load once the room has had a drink.
descriptions.Concrete Jungle Par 3's: Par 3s wedged into a city, par 54 over 1,372 yards, by the builder of the warship and moon courses. Simulator only. The holes are short and the targets are obvious, so a beginner can get round it without help, which is more than most novelty builds manage. An hour at most.
descriptions.Jurassic Par 3: The par-3 version of the Jurassic Park island, by CDrum: par 54 over 2,497 yards, dinosaurs included. It works as the second half of an afternoon that starts with the full-length Isla Nublar build. Simulator only, and short enough to finish before the light goes.
descriptions.Lost Island Par 3: A tropical par 3 from Carl's Place, par 27 over 1,206 yards: nine short holes on an invented island. The SGT regulars rate Carl's Place as the best builders working in GSPro, and this is the smallest of their three. Simulator only, and a round of about an hour.
descriptions.Moonwalk Par 3's: Par 3s on the lunar surface, par 54 over 2,006 yards. The greens are soft, which is not how the moon works, and the build makes no case for itself on that point. Simulator only, and short enough that the premise does not outstay itself.
descriptions.Redwood Run: A par-54 short course from Carl's Place, who the SGT regulars rate as the best builders working in GSPro. Invented, coastal, and the middle one of their three, which is reason enough to take all of them. Short holes, an hour, no ceremony.
descriptions.Replica Ridge: Eighteen replicas of famous par 3s in one round: the island green, the Postage Stamp and the rest, taken off their home courses and set side by side. A simulator-only build, and the quickest way to play the holes everybody has watched on television. Short enough for a beginner to enjoy.
descriptions.Bedford Springs Miniature Golf: The putting lawn at the Omni Bedford Springs, a Pennsylvania mineral-springs resort whose history runs back to the 1790s and whose Old Course was rebuilt by Donald Ross in the 1920s. 280 yards of putting over eighteen holes, which is twenty minutes. The prettiest setting in this section by a distance.
descriptions.Bucks Run Putting Island: An eighteen-hole putting course on natural grass, laid out on an island in the lake at Bucks Run in Mount Pleasant, Michigan, and reached by footbridge; the lake was a gravel quarry. Rough and bunkers are in play, but it is putter only. Good practice, and easy to hand to a guest.
descriptions.Butler Pitch & Putt: Nine holes in downtown Austin, built one at a time by the Kinser brothers on a worked-out brick company clay pit at the turn of the 1950s and run by the family for about seventy years until 2019. Wedge and putter, nothing longer. The best short-game round in this section, and a piece of old Austin.
descriptions.Day – Night Chip and Putt: The same chip-and-putt layout supplied twice, once in daylight and once under floodlights, so whichever matches the room can be loaded. 664 yards of short holes in Indiana. Chipping and putting practice with a scorecard attached, and no reason to use anything but the two shortest clubs.
descriptions.Flushing Meadows Pitch and Putt: A municipal pitch and putt in Flushing Meadows-Corona Park, the Queens ground Robert Moses had cleared out of an ash dump for the 1939 World's Fair, with the Unisphere from the 1964 fair still standing over it. Lit in the evening. Wedge golf, and about as New York as the game gets.
descriptions.Mill Creek Metroparks Putting Course: An eighteen-hole putting course in Mill Creek Park, the large municipal park that runs south out of Youngstown. Putter only, which makes it the obvious thing to point a putting camera at, and a round takes no longer than a coffee.
descriptions.Backwoods Chip n Putt: Short-game practice in the trees: 1,054 yards of chipping and putting through the woods. The build comes with a request that Birdie be left alone. Simulator only, useful for wedge work, and forgiving enough for a first-timer to get round without losing interest.
descriptions.Billy Baroo's Chip n' Putt: Named after Judge Smails's putter in Caddyshack, which sets the tone before a ball is struck. 975 yards of chipping and putting over eighteen holes, par 54, simulator only. Short-game practice with a joke on the signboard, and nothing in it that a beginner cannot handle.
descriptions.Fossil Preserve Putt Putt: Eighteen holes of mini golf in a prehistoric setting, dinosaurs and all, par 57, from the builder of the Isla Nublar course. Simulator only. Putter in hand, no technique required and no scorecard worth keeping, and the one in this section to put in front of children.
descriptions.Mulligan's Island Putt Putt (Cave): Putt-putt built on the Mulligan's Island theme in Cranston, Rhode Island, with a cave for a gimmick and a putting surface that runs through it. Eighteen holes over 244 yards, putter only, about fifteen minutes from first tee to last. A laugh after dinner rather than anything that counts as practice.
descriptions.Outdoors Putt-Putt: An invented putt-putt course that reached number twelve on a monthly chart, which for a putting build is a notable result. Eighteen holes, par 54, putter only. Something to give a guest who has never held a club, and over in twenty minutes.
descriptions.Putt Stroke Mini Golf: Synthetic-turf mini golf set in Sarasota, 231 yards of it, laid out with fairway, bunker and rough surfaces so the putter has to work off more than carpet. Eighteen holes, twenty minutes, and better practice for feel than the premise suggests.
descriptions.Putt Warehouse: Mini golf inside a warehouse in Saskatoon, with the greens running at stimp 13 indoors, which is both the joke and the difficulty. Eighteen holes, putter only. Short, silly, and harder than it sounds once the first downhill putt gets away.
descriptions.The Putting Grounds: Putting only, eighteen holes, invented. The second of the builds worth pointing a webcam putting tracker at, alongside Mill Creek, and otherwise a quiet twenty minutes of lag putting and short ones to finish. Nothing in it calls for a full swing.
descriptions.Twisted Sticks Pitch & Putt: The short half of the Twisted Sticks pair in Newland, North Carolina: 1,107 yards, par 54, wedges and a putter. The build's own fiction has it as a private club lost in time and founded in 1874, which is invention rather than history. Simulator only, and kind to a beginner.

missing.Lurid Mills 2: Fantasy build whose reference could not be identified. Name, location line and note give only a vague horror flavour and there is no known work called Lurid Mills to point at.
missing.Shale Creek: Architect and opening year unverifiable. Directory and print-on-demand pages contradict each other (Arthur Hills 2000 vs Brian Huntley 2006) with nothing from the club, and no checkable hole or event detail to write about instead.
missing.White Birch: No location on the card and no real course of this name could be matched. The card's own note says the design has not reached the course directories and the named designer is the sim builder, not an architect.
